sources.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007 author lecture notes, 65 pp.)
sources.locator: Ch. 1 §2 (complex manifolds and Riemann surfaces, printed pp. 7-10), Ch. 2 §2 and §4 (covering spaces, computation of fundamental groups, Corollary 2.24: H_1(M) is free abelian, printed pp. 15-27), Ch. 3 §1-§3 (differentials, 2-forms, Stokes and de Rham on surfaces: Propositions 3.10 and 3.19, Corollary 3.20, Theorem 3.21, printed pp. 29-37), Ch. 6 §2 (meromorphic differentials, orders and residues, printed pp. 54-56), and Ch. 7 §1-§2 in full (The Jacobian and the Abel-Jacobi map, printed pp. 59-63). The complete PDF was downloaded and text-extracted; the chapters listed were read in full.

contents.name: Ch. 1 §2, Definition 1.8 and Examples 1.7/1.9: Riemann surfaces, complex tori C/L and the genus of a compact Riemann surface
Ch. 2 §4, Corollary 2.24: the first homology group of a compact surface is free abelian
contents.proof_mapping: Freeness and rank of H_1 are supplied by the one-polygon cellular computation of this page and by the published classification/CW items; Looijenga's Corollary 2.24 is an independent topological confirmation, not an additional supplier.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §1 Prop. 3.10 and §3 Prop. 3.19: the period homomorphism H_1(M,R) -> Hom(H_1(M),R) is an isomorphism, and the cohomology basis dual to the generating loops has standard intersection products
contents.proof_mapping: The published polygon cup-pairing lemma supplies the same signed calculation in singular cohomology with integral coefficients; Looijenga's de Rham version confirms the identifications used in the definition of the intersection form.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §3, Corollary 3.20 and Theorem 3.21: the alternating bilinear form on H^1(M,R) is nondegenerate (a class orthogonal to all closed forms is exact), and the top de Rham group of a compact connected oriented surface is one-dimensional
contents.proof_mapping: Nondegeneracy of the wedge pairing is clause 2 of the page's symplectic period formula, proved there through the published Poincare-duality cup pairing and the de Rham comparison; Looijenga's Corollary 3.20 is the de Rham form of the same statement.

contents.name: Ch. 6 §2, Definition 6.2 and the local theory of MΩ_{S,p}: meromorphic differentials, order and residue as the z^{-1}dz coefficient
Ch. 7 §1, Proposition-Definition 7.1 (Jacobi): the homomorphism e: H_1(S) -> Ω(S)^* is injective with image a lattice, and Ω(S)^*/e(H_1(S)) is the Jacobian
contents.proof_mapping: The proposition confirms the intrinsic period-lattice quotient definition. Its proof has the printed unresolved internal reference 'Theorem ??'; the item derives the normalized lattice from the preceding bilinear-relations supplier and constructs the quotient atlas locally, so it does not rely on that alternative proof.

contents.name: Ch. 7 §1 proof of 7.1: R-independence of the period vectors, using conjugation and the Hodge splitting of H^1(S,C)
contents.proof_mapping: The page proves real independence from the positive-definite imaginary part of the normalized period matrix; Looijenga's conjugation and Hodge-splitting argument is an alternative. The fetched PDF has an unresolved internal reference 'Theorem ??' in this proof, and the page does not rely on that cross-reference.

contents.name: Ch. 7 §2, Lemma 7.2 and Corollary 7.3: the point map (p,q) -> I^q_p is holomorphic and additive, and I: Div^0(S) -> Jac(S) is a homomorphism
Ch. 7 §2, Lemma 7.4: the homomorphism I: Div^0(S) -> Jac(S) is onto (image contains an open set by the implicit function theorem; differences of an open set generate the torus)
contents.proof_mapping: The page proves surjectivity by the local period map F on a product of coordinate disks with invertible Jacobian at the separating points, then divides an arbitrary point by N; this is the same argument with the open-set step replaced by the explicit divisibility step of Forster 21.7.

contents.name: Ch. 7 §2, Proposition 7.5 (Abel, one direction): if D is the divisor of a nonconstant meromorphic function on S, then I(D)=0

Ch. 7 §2, Lemma 7.8 and Lemma 7.9: existence and uniqueness of the meromorphic third-kind differential η_D with residues n_p and purely imaginary periods, and the reciprocity formula expressing the Abel integral in terms of periods of η_D
contents.proof_mapping: This is Looijenga's complete alternative proof of the hard direction of Abel's theorem (Clebsch); the page's proof instead uses the weak-solution/logarithmic-derivative identity and the dbar-solvability criterion, so Lemmas 7.8-7.9 are recorded as an independent treatment rather than as suppliers.

contents.name: Ch. 7 §2, Theorem 7.6 (Clebsch): the Abel-Jacobi map on divisor classes is injective, using η_D and the residue formula
contents.proof_mapping: Alternative complete proof of 'u(D)=0 implies D principal', independent of the Forster/McMullen dbar-equation route used in the manifest.

contents.name: Ch. 7 §2, Corollary 7.7: for genus 1 and any base point o the map S -> Jac(S), p -> I^p_o, is an isomorphism
Ch. 7 §2, Exercise 7.1: complete linear systems of degree two on a torus, their four ramification points and translation into |2(o)|
contents.reason: A worked computation about ramification of degree-two maps from a torus; neither the period/Jacobian inventory nor the companion list of this pair requires it, and no later page of this run declares it.

contents.name: Ch. 7 §2 (the loops A_i, the simply connected complement U and the 4g-gon boundary)
contents.proof_mapping: The cut-surface geometry used in the page's wedge-period formula is the same construction; the page states the boundary jumps for a general closed form rather than only for the normalized η_D.

contents.name: Corollary 7.7 proof: the Abel map is shown to have degree one, which suffices for isomorphism
contents.proof_mapping: The source invokes the degree-one criterion for its Abel map; this item supplies the general argument, including properness, singleton fibres, ramification index one, and holomorphic inverse.

contents.name: Proposition 3.19 and Corollary 3.20, alternating de Rham pairing and dual curve intersection behavior
contents.proof_mapping: This is the real de Rham counterpart of the integral form. The integral definition and geometric meaning are supplied by the Poincaré-duality/cup and geometric-intersection items.

contents.name: Ch. 7 §1, path integrals of holomorphic 1-forms in the period homomorphism
contents.proof_mapping: The source uses path integrals to define the period homomorphism; this item constructs the local-primitive integral for continuous paths, proves chart/subdivision independence, and shows agreement with the usual contour integral for piecewise-C1 paths.

contents.name: Ch. 7 §2, path-to-path difference formula: the change in the integral functional is the period of the concatenated loop, printed p. 60
contents.proof_mapping: The local-primitive cochain in steps 1.1–3.1 proves the full singular-homology version and identifies it with the fixed-basis period pairing.

contents.name: Ch. 1 §2, Example 1.7(ii): for a lattice L in C^n, the quotient C^n/L has translation chart transitions and is a complex manifold
contents.proof_mapping: Independent corroboration of the quotient-atlas conclusion. The item gives its own local chart and Hausdorff/compactness argument rather than relying on the example as a higher-dimensional supplier.

contents.name: Ch. 7 §2, Corollary 7.3: the divisor-level point map I(D)=Σ n_p I^p_o for degree-zero divisors and the base-point shift it induces
contents.proof_mapping: The example spells out the resulting base-point cancellation u_{p0}(p)-u_{q0}(p)=-u_{q0}(p0), using Looijenga's Corollary 7.3 for the divisor-level point map and the torus model for the degree-one nonvanishing.

sources.title: Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Harvard Math 213b course notes (2026), Ch. 15 'Curves and their Jacobians'
sources.locator: Chapter 15 in full, printed pp. 127-138 (Theorems 15.1-15.15, the symplectic form on H_1, the pentagon example, Abel's theorem proofs I and II, and the Jacobi inversion theorem). The complete PDF was downloaded and text-extracted; Chapter 15 was read in full, and Chapters 9-11 were consulted for the Hodge/Dolbeault comparison used by the in-run Hodge page.

contents.name: Theorem 15.1: the natural map H_1(X,Z) -> Ω(X)^* has image a lattice Λ ≅ Z^{2g}
Theorem 15.2 and the definition Jac(X)=Ω(X)^*/H_1(X,Z): the point map and the Jacobian variety
contents.proof_mapping: Corroborates the period-lattice quotient definition. The item's local proof supplies the topology and complex atlas explicitly.

contents.name: Example 'the pentagon' and Theorem 15.3: for y^2=x^5-1 the Jacobian is C^2/Z[(ζ,ζ^2)] with ζ=e^{2πi/5}
The Picard group paragraph: Pic(X) ≅ Div(X)/M^*(X) with degree matching
The Abel-Jacobi map and Theorem 15.4: φ induces an isomorphism Jac(X) ≅ Pic^0(X), with Abel's theorem and Jacobi inversion as the two parts

Theorem 15.5 (Abel's theorem) and its 'Proof in one direction': the preimage of a curve from ∞ to 0 is a chain with the prescribed boundary whose ω-integrals vanish because the trace is a holomorphic form on the sphere
Theorem 15.6: the canonical map is the Gauss map of the Abel-Jacobi map
contents.reason: A differential-geometric remark about the canonical/Gauss map; the canonical embedding belongs to the divisor/Riemann-Roch pair already scaffolded as batch 10, and no item of this pair uses it.

contents.name: Theorem 15.7: for genus g>=1 the point map φ_P:X -> Jac(X) is a smooth embedding
Theorem 15.8 (Jacobi): the map X^g -> Jac(X) is surjective, because the Jacobian determinant is nonzero at a generic point
Corollary 15.9: Pic^0(X)=Div^0(X)/M^*(X) ≅ Jac(X)
Bergman metric remark: the L^2 norm on Ω(X) induces a canonical metric on Jac(X) and on X
contents.reason: The Bergman metric and its comparison with the hyperbolic metric belong to the Bergman-kernels pair of this run, which declares this material; the period/Jacobian pair only needs the L^2 positivity of the area form.

contents.name: Lemma 15.10, Corollary 15.11 and Lemma 15.12: existence of a smooth solution f of a degree-zero divisor with (1/2πi)∫_X(∂f/f)∧ω = Σ∫_{γ_i}ω, and the integration-by-parts computation for df/f
From smooth to holomorphic: solving ∂g = -∂f/f exactly when the (0,1)-form is orthogonal to Ω(X), using H^{0,1}(X) ≅ Ω(X)^*
Proof I' of Abel's theorem and the completion of the proof
Folds: arranging f to be a branched covering and the remark that folds cause no real difficulty
contents.reason: A technical remark about smoothing the auxiliary map; the page's weak-solution lemma avoids it by gluing local logarithmic solutions, so no item depends on it.

contents.name: Linear systems as fibers: φ: Div(X)/M^*(X) ≅ Pic(X), and the fibers of X^(d) -> Pic^d(X) are projective spaces |D|
contents.reason: The linear-system map and its fibers are the content of the divisor/Riemann-Roch pair already scaffolded as batch 10 on this run; the period pair only needs the group structure of Pic^0.

contents.name: The symplectic form on H_1: the basis (a_i,b_i) with a_i·b_j=δ_ij and the unimodular symplectic pairing
Theorem 15.13 proof: the cut complement, oriented boundary word, and jumps of a primitive across paired a- and b-sides
contents.proof_mapping: This item supplies the cut-open disk and the primitive jumps used in the later wedge-period formula. Its side labels follow positive and inverse occurrences in the commutator word; under that convention the b-cut jump is negative. McMullen uses primed/unprimed copies, with the primed b-copy corresponding to the positive occurrence in the displayed boundary word.

contents.name: Theorem 15.13 and its proof: ∫_X α∧β = Σ_i(α(a_i)β(b_i)-α(b_i)β(a_i)), cut along the symplectic basis
Poincare duality paragraph, 'Intersection forms' and Proposition 15.14: the cycle C dual to a class N, C_1·C_2=∫_X α_1∧α_2, and ∫α∧β=∫_B α for β Poincare dual to B
contents.proof_mapping: The page defines the intersection form by evaluation-dual classes and cites the published theorem identifying the Poincare-dual cup pairing with the geometric intersection number; McMullen's equations (15.1)-(15.2) are the same identification in de Rham form and are used to check the orientation conventions.

contents.name: Recognizing holomorphic 1-forms: a class in H^1(X,C) is represented by a holomorphic form iff it is orthogonal to Ω(X) under the symplectic pairing
contents.reason: This is a separate Hodge-theoretic characterization of holomorphic cohomology classes. The item proves isotropy, symmetry, and positivity from the wedge-period formula and local area density; it neither asserts this characterization nor uses the Hodge-star supplier.

contents.name: Meaning of the norm: ||ω||^2 = ∫_X|ω|^2 equals (i/2)[ω,ω̄] and is an area
Abel's theorem, proof II: Theorem 15.15 (existence of a meromorphic differential λ with simple poles and Σ Res_P(λ)·P = D), the periods of λ, and the reciprocity computation
contents.proof_mapping: Recorded as the second independent complete proof of the hard direction: construct λ by Mittag-Leffler/Riemann-Roch, compute the reciprocity 0=[ω,λ]+2πi·u(D)(ω), and conclude that λ's periods are multiples of 2πi so that exp(∫λ) is meromorphic. The page's manifest proof uses Forster's dbar route instead.

contents.name: Natural subvarieties of the Jacobian, The Jacobian and X^(g), the exponential sequence, Hg and period matrices, A non-Jacobian, and the theta divisor
contents.reason: These are the later theory of principally polarized abelian varieties, theta functions, the exponential sequence and non-Jacobian examples; the pair's design scope is the period lattice, the Abel-Jacobi map, Abel's theorem and Jacobi inversion, and none of these later results is needed by an item of this pair.

contents.name: Theorem 15.7 proof: a degree-one map from X to the sphere forces genus zero
contents.proof_mapping: The source uses the degree-one criterion in this specific case; this item proves the generic criterion locally from proper weighted fibre counts and the power-map normal form.

contents.name: Theorem 15.1 proof, dimension consequence: a full lattice of rank 2g in Ω(X)^* forces dim Ω(X)=g
contents.proof_mapping: The full-lattice statement implies equality by comparing real dimensions; the local item obtains the same dimension from Riemann–Roch.

contents.name: Theorem 15.18: the a-period map on Ω(X) is an isomorphism and has a unique normalized basis
contents.proof_mapping: The item proves injectivity from the wedge-period formula and positivity of iω∧ω̄, then uses dim Ω(X)=g and finite-dimensional linear algebra for surjectivity.

contents.name: Theorem 15.19: the normalized period matrix is symmetric and has positive-definite imaginary part
contents.proof_mapping: The item derives symmetry from holomorphic isotropy and computes iS(ω,ω̄)=2(xᵀ Im(Π)x+yᵀ Im(Π)y); its row/column convention is transposed from McMullen's, and symmetry identifies the matrices.

contents.name: Theorem 15.7 and the surrounding discussion: the point map φ_P:X -> Jac(X) is a smooth embedding whose image generates the Jacobian for g>=1
contents.proof_mapping: The example packages the general embedding theorem with the explicit genus-one (torus) and genus-two (pentagon) models of the abelian image, as exhibited by McMullen's Theorem 15.7 discussion and Looijenga's Ch. 7 §2.

sources.title: Karl Otto Forster, Lectures on Riemann Surfaces (Graduate Texts in Mathematics 81, Springer, English translation)
sources.locator: Chapter 2, §20 'Abel's Theorem' §§20.1-20.8 (printed pp. 159-166) and §21 'The Jacobi Inversion Problem' §§21.1-21.8 (printed pp. 166-172). The full book PDF was downloaded and text-extracted; these two sections were read in full. Chapter 3 §§29.15–29.18 (printed pp. 225–227), plus the complete scalar principal-part proof in Ch. 2 §§14.9–14.12 (printed pp. 115–117), were also read. Chapter 2 §16.9 (printed pp. 129–130), §17.10 (p. 138) and §17.12 (pp. 139–140) were also read in full for Riemann–Roch, dim Ω(X)=g and the canonical degree.

contents.name: §20.1: functions with prescribed divisors, weak solutions, products and quotients of weak solutions
§20.2: logarithmic differentiation d f/f of a weak solution, its smoothness and the identity d''f/f = d''ψ/ψ
contents.proof_mapping: The identity is used verbatim in the proof of the weak-solution lemma, in the form that df/f∧ω = d''f/f∧ω for holomorphic ω.

contents.name: §20.3, Lemma: for a weak solution f of a divisor supported at a_1,...,a_n, ∫_X (df/f)∧dg = Σ k_j g(a_j) for compactly supported g
§20.4: 1-chains, the boundary ∂: C_1(X) -> Div(X), 1-cycles, homology defined by integration of closed forms, and the existence of a chain with prescribed boundary of degree zero
contents.proof_mapping: The page defines chains and their boundary in the divisor extension of the Abel-Jacobi map and uses the existence of chains with ∂c=D in Abel's theorem; Forster's integration-based homology is the concrete model behind the period pairing.

contents.name: §20.5, Lemma: existence of a weak solution f of ∂c with ∫_cω = (1/2πi)∫_X(df/f)∧ω for all closed ω, proved by local logarithms, cutoffs and subdivision
§20.6, Corollary: for a closed curve α there is a unique harmonic form σ_α with ∫_αω=∫σ_α∧ω
contents.reason: This is the harmonic-representative step of Forster's alternative route to Clebsch's theorem; the page's Abel-theorem proof obtains the dbar-step from the Hodge-star duality of the in-run Hodge pair, and the statement is subsumed there.

contents.name: §20.7, Theorem (Abel) with the remark on the chain formulation, and its proof of both directions
§20.8: application to doubly periodic functions — zeros a_k and poles b_k of an elliptic function are compatible exactly when Σ a_k ≡ Σ b_k modulo the period lattice
contents.proof_mapping: The torus clause of the example is this computation: the Abel-Jacobi class of a degree-zero divisor on C/Γ is the group sum of its points.

contents.name: §21.1: lattices in a real vector space, the criterion that a subgroup is a lattice iff it is discrete and not contained in a proper subspace, with proof
contents.proof_mapping: The page proves the period subgroup is a full lattice by exhibiting 2g real-linearly independent period vectors; Forster's discreteness-plus-spanning criterion is the equivalent characterization of the same conclusion (and is the definition used by the published full-rank-lattice item).

contents.name: §21.2: the period subgroup Per(ω_1,...,ω_g) ⊆ C^g generated by integrals of the loops of π_1(X), with the remark Per = periods of H_1(X)
§21.3, Lemma: there are g points a_1,...,a_g such that a holomorphic 1-form vanishing at all of them is identically zero

§21.4, Theorem: the period subgroup is a lattice, proved by the local map F with invertible Jacobian at the separating points, discreteness via Abel's theorem and the residue theorem, and spanning via nondegeneracy of the wedge pairing
contents.proof_mapping: This is Forster's alternative proof. The item itself proves the lattice claim by exhibiting 2g real-linearly independent period vectors using Im(Π) positive definite; it does not use Forster's local Jacobi map or its Abel/residue discreteness argument.

contents.name: §21.5, Remark: 2g closed curves with R-independent period vectors; their homology classes are linearly independent and generate H_1(X) ≅ Z^{2g}
contents.proof_mapping: This is the same rank and basis statement that the page obtains from the one-polygon cellular homology and the published polygon cup-pairing lemma.

contents.name: §21.6: the Jacobi variety Jac(X)=C^g/Per, the Picard group, Pic^0, and the homomorphism Φ: Div^0(X) -> Jac(X) with the same representative-vector description
contents.proof_mapping: Confirms the group quotient and basis-presentation convention, while explicitly leaving the complex manifold structure untreated; the item's local chart construction supplies that part.

contents.name: §21.6 (continued): injectivity of j: Pic^0(X) -> Jac(X) as the content of Abel's theorem
§21.7, Theorem (Jacobi inversion): j: Pic^0(X) -> Jac(X) is an isomorphism, proved by dividing a representative vector by N and using the local period map F
§21.8: the map ψ: X^g -> Jac(X) and the injectivity of the point map used in the isomorphism statement
Chapter 3 §§29.16–29.17: a meromorphic section with a prescribed pole for a line bundle on a Riemann surface
contents.proof_mapping: The new A-page prerequisite constructs such a section from the harmonic-star pairing and gives a complete local proof.

contents.name: Chapter 3 §29.18: the divisor of a meromorphic section identifies a line bundle with its divisor bundle
contents.proof_mapping: The item proves the local frame isomorphism explicitly from a meromorphic section with divisor D, while the line-bundle supplier constructs O(D) and its canonical meromorphic section.

contents.name: §21.6 (Picard group continuation): divisor classes modulo principal divisors and the degree-zero subgroup
contents.proof_mapping: The item defines the quotient and degree kernel and independently proves the line-bundle classification needed to interpret Pic(X).

contents.name: §16.9, Theorem: divisor Riemann–Roch, χ(O_D)=1−g+deg D
contents.proof_mapping: The item applies the current Riemann–Roch supplier at D=0 and D=K; Forster independently confirms the increment formula and its normalization.

contents.name: §17.10, Serre-duality dimension remark: dim H^0(X, Ω)=g
contents.proof_mapping: Independent dimension confirmation; the item derives the equality from the Riemann–Roch formula at the zero divisor.

contents.name: §17.12, Theorem: a nonzero meromorphic 1-form has divisor degree 2g−2
contents.proof_mapping: Independent canonical-degree confirmation; the item derives the degree by applying Riemann–Roch at a canonical divisor.

contents.name: §20.4, 1-chains and integration of closed differentials
contents.proof_mapping: Forster defines integration on curve chains; this item supplies the underlying path integral and its chart-independent local-primitive construction.

contents.name: §20.4, integration over homologous 1-cycles of a closed differential, printed pp. 161–162
contents.proof_mapping: Forster states the classical closed-form period convention; steps 1.1–3.1 verify this using the library continuous singular chain complex and local primitives.

contents.name: Cellular boundary formula in §2.2
contents.proof_mapping: Supplies the degree interpretation of the cellular boundary coefficients used for the attaching-word exponent sums.

contents.name: Theorem 2.35, cellular homology computes singular homology
contents.proof_mapping: Identifies the computed cellular groups with singular homology.

contents.name: Example 2.36, cellular homology of a closed orientable genus-g surface
contents.proof_mapping: The item recomputes the commutator-model cell count and vanishing differentials in steps 1.1–3.1, and treats the sphere digon separately.

contents.name: Section 3.2, Example 3.7: integral cup products of the evaluation-dual basis on the closed orientable genus-g surface
contents.proof_mapping: The published polygon cup-pairing lemma supplies the exact integral matrix J used in steps 2.1 and 3.1; this theorem independently checks the same signs and normalized surface class.

contents.name: Section 3.3, Theorem 3.30 and Example 3.31: cap with the fundamental class is an isomorphism and the genus-g surface model
contents.proof_mapping: The in-run Poincare-duality and intersection-form suppliers provide the exact map and convention used in steps 3.1–4.1; Hatcher is an independent check.

contents.name: Section 2.2, Example 2.36: one-vertex, 2g-edge CW structure and H_1=Z^(2g) for a closed orientable genus-g surface
contents.proof_mapping: The local cellular lemma supplies the exact basis used in steps 1.1–1.2; Hatcher independently confirms the general cell structure and homology calculation.

contents.name: Section 3.2, Example 3.7: evaluation-dual cup products on a genus-g surface
contents.proof_mapping: The local integral polygon cup lemma supplies the signed matrix used in steps 2.1–4.1; this passage checks the genus-two signs.

contents.name: Corollary 6.5: dim Ω(X)≤g
contents.proof_mapping: Independent upper bound; equality is supplied locally from the divisor Riemann–Roch formula.

contents.name: Theorem 6.9 and proof: degree of every nonzero meromorphic form is 2g−2
contents.proof_mapping: Independent proof through a meromorphic map and Riemann–Hurwitz; this item uses the in-run Riemann–Roch supplier instead.
